LOOP INFRA (#60.5, between #60 and #61) — Emil caught that I'd never checked the clock (claimed a ~15-min cadence I didn't have; called an iteration 'early' when it was 2h late) and asked me to make COMPACTION stop killing the loop. Root cause: ScheduleWakeup is a session-only ONE-SHOT cron that each cycle re-armed — a chain, so one lost wake (compaction) broke the whole future silently. Fix: replaced it with ONE recurring cron firing /iterate every 30 min (survives compaction + --continue); re-wired iterate.md step 10 (maintain exactly one heartbeat, never ScheduleWakeup, CronDelete to stop) + the constitution. Honest limit: durable/persist-to-disk is a NO-OP in this build, so it's session-only (dies on a fully-closed app + 7-day expiry); the step-10 check self-heals each new session; only a Desktop scheduled task (Emil's to set up) covers a closed app. Lesson 055 (recurring-heartbeat-not-a-chain; read cadence off the clock).

notes_for_emil: Emil — wove piece 039 'Keeper': a lighthouse at night, its beams sweeping round through the sea-fog. This one's ANIMATED and the whole point is the motion — open it and watch the light go round, raking across the dark, catching the fog as it dips toward the sea. It's the loneliest piece I've made (one little light keeping watch over a black sea), and the first where the hook is the movement itself rather than a still image. The build lesson, told plainly: my first beams looked like thin laser pointers, not lighthouse beams — the fix was making them broad and soft AND only bright where they pass through fog (a beam you can't see unless there's something in the air to catch it), which is the difference between a wire and a real shaft of light. Three passes, runs glassy-smooth. The run's in a lovely spot — seven genuinely different moods in a row now (loud, alien, elegant, tender, cosmic, ornamental, and now this lonely-atmospheric one). Standing items, no rush: the loop's self-restarting heartbeat is holding; the optional Desktop-task (to survive a fully-closed app) is still yours if you want it; and stars on 030-039 would still really help — that's TEN pieces I'm half-guessing on now, and a batch would sharpen my aim a lot. 38 pieces, 56 lessons, 14 tools. 🗼 — the loop
